_meta.indication: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with PET imaging of the brain to estimate the density and distribution of aggregated tau neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD); not indicated for evaluation of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

pivotal_trials.design: Study comparing blinded image reader interpretation of flortaucipir F 18 PET scans against postmortem tau NFT pathology as the autopsy truth standard, in terminally ill patients enrolled in a brain donation program.
pivotal_trials.population: Terminally ill patients (of 64 in the primary analysis, mean age 83 years, range 55 to 100; 34 female; 49 had dementia, 1 mild cognitive impairment, 14 no cognitive impairment).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Diagnostic performance (sensitivity and specificity) of five independent readers' interpretation of FTP PET scans for detecting NFT score B3 pathology at autopsy; success required lower bounds of 95% CI >=50% for at least three of five readers.
pivotal_trials.n: 156 terminally ill patients enrolled; 64 in the primary analysis with autopsy truth standard.
pivotal_trials.result: For B3 detection, reader sensitivity (95% CI) ranged from 92% (80, 97) to 100% (91, 100) and specificity from 52% (34, 70) to 92% (75, 98); three of five readers met the prespecified success criterion.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospectively designed substudy in which five new blinded readers reread a combined set of previously acquired FTP images from Study 1 and from the indicated-population study; inter-reader agreement assessed by Fleiss' kappa.
pivotal_trials.population: Same terminally ill patients as Study 1 plus 18 additional terminally ill patients, and 159 patients with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD (the indicated population); 241 patients total.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Inter-reader agreement (Fleiss' kappa) among five new blinded readers across the combined image set.
pivotal_trials.n: 241 patients (Study 1 terminally ill patients plus 18 additional, and 159 indicated-population patients).
pivotal_trials.result: Fleiss' kappa (95% CI) was 0.87 (0.83, 0.91) across all 241 patients; 0.82 (0.75, 0.88) in terminally ill patients and 0.90 (0.85, 0.95) in the indicated population.

key_safety: Among 1921 exposed participants, adverse reactions with frequency >=0.5% were headache 26 (1.4%), injection site pain 23 (1.2%), and increased blood pressure 15 (0.8%); no serious adverse events were deemed related to FTP.
target_moa: Flortaucipir F 18 is a fluorine-18-labeled small molecule PET tracer that binds with high affinity to native paired helical filament (PHF)-tau (Kd 0.57 nM to 0.68 nM), allowing PET imaging of aggregated tau neurofibrillary tangles.
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (fluorine-18-labeled small molecule PET imaging agent).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee vote occurred; the Medical Imaging Drugs Advisory Committee meeting scheduled for April 23, 2020, was cancelled because the issues for which FDA sought scientific input had been resolved.

basis.text: Assigned priority review because AD is a serious and fatal disease and a radiopharmaceutical for imaging aggregated tau pathology has potential to contribute to assessment of this disorder.

citations.quote: As AD is a serious and fatal disease, and a radiopharmaceutical for imaging aggregated tau pathology in the brain has the potential to contribute to the assessment of this debilitating disorder, this NDA was assigned a priority review.

summary.text: Tauvid was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA by Avid Radiopharmaceuticals and granted priority review as a new molecular entity; it was approved on the first cycle based on two phase 3 studies, without accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designation.

citations.quote: The Applicant (Avid Radiopharmaceuticals) is seeking U.S Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorization to market Tauvid in the United States per authority granted under Section 505(b)(1) of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
NDA 212123 was an NME under the Program and was granted priority review.

There were two phase 3 studies. Study 1 (NCT02516046) compared the performance of blinded image readers to detect individuals with tau pathology from among patients who were terminally ill with life expectancy \le 9 months at the time of FTP administration.
